status: independent complete underline-class review; supersedes plain-n findings in independent-first-reading-review.json
notation: The printed horizontal low line is encoded as U+0332 on each covered n. This preserves visible typography without assigning a phonetic value. The PDF text layer omits the line; round underdots elsewhere remain U+0323.

corrections.evidence: Original p19 accusative line: separate low line directly under n in both words; PDF page19 crop Rect(92,395,230,435) at 9x.
Original p19 genitive line: continuous low line spans both adjacent n glyphs in each word; page19 crop Rect(92,540,220,725) at 9x.
Original p19 locative line: continuous low line spans both n glyphs; same 9x crop.

Original p20 pronoun table, full-page image and 7x Rect(92,218,350,319). The low line covers the final n of naanu, en, niinu, taan, tan, avnu and both adjacent n glyphs of ivnnu. Other pronoun cells have no such low line.
Original p20 interrogative table, 6x Rect(90,310,355,640): low line spans both n in eennei and n in evnu; other cells have none.

negative_controls: p19 -in- prose increment has no separate low line
p20 plural-pronoun nānke/nanke, nīnke/ninke and other right-column cells show no low line
p20 gender example eṇṇukūsu has round underdots under consonants rather than horizontal low lines
p21 negative, causative, hortative and 17 lexical-list source forms show no horizontal low line under n

additional_omission.disposition: audit-only documentary/local term; source does not explicitly identify this as Cholanaickan-language speech
additional_omission.note: Retain exact p19 prose locator and English explanatory meaning without inventing a target lemma.

other_scope_findings: p20 -tti is reconstructed South Dravidian comparison, -cci is explicitly retained by Tamil/Kodagu/Kannada; they are not independently attested Cholanaickan feminine forms
p20 -annu is a stem-ending condition in the vocative paragraph, not itself a vocative suffix
